capabilities: Launch a Neovim instance in a terminal when Obsidian starts
Open the active Obsidian file as a buffer in the listening Neovim instance
Focus an existing Neovim buffer instead of opening a duplicate
Send new Neovim buffers back to Obsidian via obsidian-bridge.nvim and obsidian-local-rest-api
extras: README warns the plugin doesn't work when Obsidian is installed via flatpak, reports an infinite-loop bug when files are renamed or deleted from Obsidian while their buffer is open in Neovim, and recommends doing file operations from Neovim. Includes edge-case notes such as a specific terminal path for Ghostty on macOS.
intentEvidence: I know Obsidian has vim bindings, but I've built up my own Neovim config
motivation: The author prefers editing in their own customized Neovim setup rather than Obsidian's built-in vim bindings.
problem: Obsidian's built-in vim mode can't use a user's full personal Neovim configuration for editing.

relations.evidence: The obsidian.nvim plugin, also highly recommended in general for interacting with Obsidian vaults from Neovim
The obsidian-bridge.nvim along side the obsidian-local-rest-api, this is what enables to communication
The obsidian-bridge.nvim along side the obsidian-local-rest-api, this is what enables to communication

summary: Neovim bridge that opens every file you view in Obsidian as a buffer in a running external Neovim instance.
